Lets Child Lock use the volume buttons and keep your child in the app

While the lock is on, Child Lock uses this to notice the volume-button pattern, block the back button and swipes, close the notifications panel, and return to the app you handed over. While off, it only notices which app is open and whether a call or video is playing, so it can lock automatically. It never reads or stores what is on screen. (Where the optional “Skip ads” feature exists and is switched on, it reads button labels in the app you handed over, and nothing else.)

Child Lock uses Android’s accessibility feature as a parental lock, not as an accessibility aid.

While locked, it:
• Notices the volume-button pattern that unlocks
• Blocks the back button and home/back swipes
• Closes the notifications panel and returns to the app

While unlocked, it only notices which app is open, and whether a call or video is playing, for automatic locking.

It never reads, stores or sends what is on your screen.

(If this copy of Child Lock offers “Skip ads for them”, that one feature is off unless you turn it on, and when on it reads button labels in the app you handed over so it can tap “Skip ad”. The Play Store version does not include it.)

Next, switch on “Child Lock helper” and tap Allow.

Lets the volume buttons lock and unlock, and keeps your child inside the app. Found under Accessibility in Android settings.
Android said “Restricted setting”? Open App info, tap the ⋮ menu, choose “Allow restricted settings”, then try again.
Android added a floating button you don’t need. Open the helper’s page and switch off “Child Lock helper shortcut”.
Press up, then down. The same presses lock and unlock, no touching the screen.

If that ever fails, hold two opposite corners of the screen.
If that ever fails, tap the screen three times with three fingers.
Press volume %1$s. You’ll see “Child Lock on”. Do it while your video, call or game is on screen.
Tap Child Lock in Quick Settings, or use the button above.
Press volume %1$s again. You’ll see “Child Lock off”.
Hold one finger in each corner until the phone buzzes.
Hold the small lock icon until the keypad appears, then enter your PIN.
Hold both volume buttons together until the phone buzzes.
Child Lock can turn on by itself, for example when a video call connects or a video goes full screen. A short countdown gives you time to hand over.
Tap an app to add it. You choose when it locks next, and can change it any time.
If you unlock and the same thing happens again, like the video going full screen again, Child Lock locks again.

While locked, if a “Skip ad” button appears in the app you handed over, Child Lock taps it. Never the ad itself, and never “Skip intro”. To do this it reads button labels in that one app; nothing is stored or sent.

Everything automatic: locking by itself when a call connects or a video goes full screen, locking again after you unlock, and skipping ads.\n\nThe lock itself, the volume buttons and every safety feature stay free, always.
These automatic extras are still being finished, so they are unlocked for now and nothing is for sale yet.\n\nThe lock itself, the volume buttons and every safety feature will always be free.
Child Lock unlocks itself when the time is up, so the phone always comes back to you.
Lock this screen and practise unlocking. A practice lock always ends by itself after a minute, so you cannot get stuck.
Purchases arrive with the Play Store release.
Preview as a free user (test builds only)
The screen won’t dim or turn off while locked.
The video stays put when the phone is tilted.
Keep my child inside the app
The back button and the notifications panel do nothing while locked, and the app comes straight back if they get out. Needs the Child Lock helper.

The swipes do nothing at all. Off by default, because it works by switching on the same mode a screen reader uses, and while that is on the corner hold cannot work: the backup unlock becomes a three-finger triple tap instead.
If it gets pulled down, it closes straight away.
If your child reaches the home screen, the app comes straight back.
If anything goes wrong, restart the phone: it always starts unlocked, and the power button always works.
Open source. No ads, no accounts, nothing leaves your phone.
